title: Packages installed at runtime extend Connect's PWA config exactly like build-time packages, with start_url and scope protected and .phd/.phdm first-registered
content:
The service worker serves `manifest.webmanifest` dynamically and reads its runtime-caching / navigate-fallback contributions from IndexedDB `ph-pwa` (mirrored by `BrowserPackageManager.#syncPwaFragments`). So a package installed **at runtime** contributes its manifest members, overridden scalars, `runtimeCaching` rules and `navigateFallbackDenylist` patterns without a rebuild — the same way build-time packages do.

Two guardrails distinguish runtime from build-time contributions: the manifest merge is fragment-wins **except `start_url` and `scope`**, which are protected so an end-user-installed package cannot re-scope the app; and the built-in `.phd` / `.phdm` OS file associations stay first-registered. Timing caveats apply to both kinds: `file_handlers` / `launch_handler` are captured by the OS at PWA install time (Chrome re-reads on its own periodic check, never mid-session; content-based routing opens `.phd`/`.phdm` regardless), and `runtimeCaching` / `navigateFallbackDenylist` are read at worker startup, taking full effect on the worker's next activation.

Only `globPatterns`, `globIgnores` and `maximumFileSizeToCacheInBytes` remain build-time only — they drive the workbox precache list baked at build. The manifest's `categories` is not authored anywhere in Connect's config; it is derived by unioning the top-level `category` of every contributing `powerhouse.manifest.json`.

_Source: apps/connect/RUNTIME-CONFIG.md (Powerhouse v6.2.2-dev.74)._
